title: The Crown
logline: An iron crown passes through four ages and four falls, and outlives every king who believed it was his.
look: Hero-object cinematography: one raking key light in darkness, drifting dust; each age has its own palette (bronze torchlight, candle gold, gaslight red, electric blue-white), ending in cool museum light. Hero holds, speed ramps, impact flashes.
narrator: male, elderly, low pitch, british accent
A grave historian, deliberate and dry
music: Deep taiko and low brass for each coronation; a metallic clang and silence for each fall; a choir pad that thins with every age; museum room tone at the end.

shots.direction: ECU macro · slow orbit · fade in — the iron crown in darkness, one raking light, dust in the beam
CU 85mm · rise · cut — the crown rises into light (hero hold)
WS 35mm · locked · impact flash — age one: torches, bronze light, the crown set upon a throne
CU · speed ramp to slow motion · cut — it falls and rolls across stone; clang flash
WS 35mm · push · cut — age two: candles and gold; the crown rises again
CU · slow motion · cut — it falls, rolling through smoke
WS 35mm · push · cut — age three: gaslight and red banners; it rises
ECU · impact flash · cut — it falls; a jewel cracks and shatters
WS 35mm · newsreel flicker · cut — age four: harsh electric light; it rises
CU · long fall into darkness · cut — it drops out of frame; silence
WS 50mm · slow push · dissolve — a museum: the crown in a glass case; a child's reflection passes in the glass
CU 85mm · hold · cut — the crown, cracked and dulled; a small placard: CROWN OF AN UNKNOWN KING
CU · light fades · cut to black — the gallery light switches off

narration.text: Every king who wore it believed it was his.
The first held it for forty years.
The third, for a single night.
The fourth never told us his name.
Now it belongs to the glass, and to a child who will forget it by dinner.
Crowns outlive kings. That is all they do.
